docRequirement: troubleshoot-install.md:664 binds the value of `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` to a file whose name is one of exactly four: `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`. "Claude Code accepts only a file named `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`; with any other name, such as Git for Windows' `git-bash.exe` launcher, it ignores the variable and auto-detects Git Bash as if it were unset, logging a warning visible with `--debug`." The same line adds that a path that does not exist gets that same fallback-plus-warning, and version-gates the whole rule with `{/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}` (before 2.1.219 any existing file was used with no name check, and a missing path exited at startup).
current: One validator gates every path we ever write into that variable, and it accepts a single name. `packages/server-core/src/services/git-bash.ts:8` is `isGitBashExecutablePath = /(?:^|[\\/])bash\.exe$/i.test(filePath.trim())`; `validateGitBashPath` (:15) refuses anything else at :18-19 with `{ valid: false, error: 'Path must point to bash.exe' }`, then requires the file to exist (:22-30). `isUsableGitBashPath` (:36) is the same predicate without the message. Three live call paths depend on it, and there are two duplicated copies of the handler. (1) Onboarding SET_PATH: `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:265-274` — a failed validation returns `{ success: false, error }` and nothing is persisted or exported; the identical handler for the desktop app is `apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:189-198` (its `registerSystemCoreHandlers` is a full duplicate of server-core's, wired at :442, while the server-core one is wired for headless in `registerCoreRpcHandlers` (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/index.ts`)). (2) Auto-detect CHECK: `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:199-248` / `apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:123-172` — a persisted path that fails revalidation is dropped by `clearGitBashPath()` (:219 / :143), then four hardcoded `...\Git\bin\bash.exe` candidates (:206-211 / :130-135) and a `where bash` result (:230-244 / :154-168) are probed, and only on success is `process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` assigned (:216, :224, :238 / :140, :148, :162) or deleted (:246 / :170). (3) Startup revalidation: `apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:596-606` — an invalid persisted path is cleared, the env var deleted, and `Cleared invalid persisted Git Bash path:` logged. The Browse dialog filters to `extensions: ['exe']` (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:253`, `apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:177`), so the two extension-less documented names cannot even be picked. The refusal is surfaced verbatim in the UI: `apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useOnboarding.ts:737-751` puts `result.error` into `errorMessage`, rendered red at `apps/electron/src/renderer/components/onboarding/GitBashWarning.tsx:115-117`. The narrowing is locked by `apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/git-bash.test.ts:21` (`isGitBashExecutablePath('/tmp/git/bin/sh.exe')` must be `false`) and :31 (the exact error string). The consumer we actually ship applies no name check at all: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.183 `bridge.mjs` reads `if(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH){if(existsSync(...))return process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH; console.error(`Claude Code was unable to find CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH path "..."`),process.exit(1)}` — i.e. the pre-2.1.219 rule.
divergence: The env var name, the value we write (a full path) and the existence requirement are all correct; only the accepted-filename predicate is wrong, and it is wrong by being a strict subset. We accept `{bash.exe}`; the page specifies `{bash.exe, sh.exe, bash, sh}`. So `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe` — and the extension-less `bash`/`sh` — are refused by us and accepted by Claude and by the SDK build we bundle. Two second-order deltas ride on the same predicate: the Browse dialog's `extensions: ['exe']` filter makes the extension-less half of the enum unselectable even if the validator widened, and our reaction to a rejected name is a hard user-facing error at SET_PATH rather than the documented silent fallback-plus-`--debug`-warning (at CHECK and at startup we do fall back, but we additionally delete the persisted value, which the page does not ask for). The existence half of the validator must NOT be relaxed toward the page's "missing path also just warns": that rule is min-version 2.1.219, the bundled SDK 0.3.183 still `process.exit(1)`s on a missing path, so our existence check is protective and stays.

userImpact: Windows only, and only when Git Bash is not at a standard `...\Git\bin\bash.exe`. A user in that position opens the onboarding Git Bash step, types or browses to the shell Git actually gave them — `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe`, or a portable/MSYS layout whose shell is `sh.exe` — presses "Use this path", and gets the red inline error "Path must point to bash.exe" (GitBashWarning.tsx:116). Onboarding will not advance past the step (useOnboarding.ts:318), so the user is stuck being told to install Git they already have, on a path the SDK we spawn would have accepted without complaint. The Browse dialog compounds it: filtered to `*.exe`, the extension-less `bash`/`sh` cannot even be selected, so the file picker shows nothing usable in that layout. If such a path ever did get persisted, the next launch silently drops it (index.ts:602-604, warning only in the main log) and onboarding re-prompts. On macOS and Linux nothing is observable — CHECK returns `{ found: true }` immediately (`.../rpc/system.ts:202-204`). Exposure is genuinely narrow because a normal Git for Windows install does ship `bin\bash.exe` and is auto-detected, which is why this has not been reported.
